name: Eli Lilly

header.one_liner: The incretin franchise: volume is still exploding, price per unit is falling faster, and the multiple already assumes the volume wins.
header.thesis: Q3 revenue grew 39% on 53% more volume and 15% lower prices, and Lilly raised 2026 revenue guidance by $5.5B to $91B to $92B. Two of our tripwires crossed: US price fell 7% and gross margin dipped below 85%. The base case fades growth to 18% a year and compresses the P/E toward 24x; the bear tail is fat, so the probability-weighted return falls short of the hurdle. The central debate is still price erosion versus volume.

base.eps_label: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS, midpoint of updated guidance $35.00 to $36.00 (includes $3.03 of Q2 and $4.57 of Q3 acquired IPR&D; about $43 before those charges)
base.rev_label: FY2026 revenue, midpoint of raised guidance $91B to $92B

rev_cagr.why: Q3 revenue +39%: volume +53%, price -15% (US volume +41%, price -7%; outside the US volume +76%, price -29%). About $900M of Q3 revenue was one-off (Jardiance milestones, rebate estimate changes). The base case fades growth from the high 30s toward the high teens as price erosion widens. This is the engine's judgment.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 35% on guided EPS, which carries $7.60 a share of acquired IPR&D from Q2 and Q3. Before those charges it is about 42%. The base case lands at 40% as one-off charges fall away, offset by price erosion; non-GAAP gross margin was 84.4% in Q3.

share_chg.why: Guidance assumes about 894M diluted shares, unchanged from mid-year. Lilly repurchased $2.4B in Q1 (call); later quarters were not stated. Buybacks roughly offset dilution.
share_chg.source: Lilly Q3 2026 release (share assumption); Q1 2026 call

exit_pe.why: Current multiple is about 41x guided 2026 EPS, or about 33x before this year's acquired IPR&D charges. Large pharmaceutical growth names have historically traded between 16x and 30x. The base case assumes a growth premium that narrows as volume growth slows. The bear case prices a reset in US pricing.

pillars.title: Volume is the story, price is the cost
pillars.claim: Volume +53% against price -15% means the franchise is growing by getting cheaper per dose and bigger in aggregate. US price fell 7%, up from 3% in Q2, so the ex-US pattern is starting to show at home.
pillars.test: Does US realised price stay within -8% a year while volume grows above 30%?

pillars.title: Margins are very high but slipped
pillars.claim: Non-GAAP gross margin was 84.4%, below Q2's level, and $4.2B of acquired IPR&D cut operating margin to about 35%. R&D held at 17% of revenue.
pillars.test: Does non-GAAP gross margin recover above 85% as Foundayo scales?

pillars.title: The pipeline widens the franchise
pillars.claim: Retatrutide beat Ozempic head to head in type 2 diabetes, with BLA planned for Q1 2027; Foundayo is launching globally; newer immunology, oncology and neuroscience products doubled.

evidence.t: Retatrutide Phase 3: more than double the weight loss of Ozempic's highest approved dose

pillars.test: Is the retatrutide BLA submitted on schedule?

pillars.title: Guidance rose on revenue, not EPS
pillars.claim: Revenue guide rose $5.5B to $91B to $92B and underlying EPS by $4.07, but the EPS range fell to $35.00 to $36.00 because of $4.57 of Q3 acquired IPR&D.

evidence.t: EPS guide $35.00 to $36.00 from $35.50 to $36.50; performance margin raised to 52.0% to 52.5%

pillars.test: Does acquired IPR&D stay a one-off or become a recurring charge?

variant.street: The market prices a long runway of incretin growth at about 41x this year's EPS and a market value near $1.3T.
variant.ours: The engine leans negative: the base case roughly earns the hurdle but the bear tail is fat, and two of four tripwires crossed in Q3 even as revenue beat. Three of four drivers are judgment, so this is the position to challenge hardest on price erosion and the multiple.
variant.could_be_wrong: If volume keeps compounding near 50% and US price stabilises around -7%, the bull case is understated.
variant.would_change_mind: US realised price falling more than 8% a year, or retatrutide delayed beyond 2027.

moat.summary: Patent-protected incretin franchise with manufacturing scale; buyers (wholesalers and PBMs) and government pricing are the weak spot.
moat.detail: Existing Porter card (FY2025 10-K) rates Lilly Moderate because buyer power is high.

quality.leverage_note: Total debt about $49.5B at 30 September, down from $54.9B at 30 June, after $18.2B of business development cash in nine months (third-party tally of the 10-Q).
quality.incentive_note: Acquired IPR&D of $4.2B in Q3 alone ($7.6 a share across Q2 and Q3); ask whether it is a recurring cost of staying ahead.
checks: About $900M of Q3 revenue was one-off: $410M of Jardiance milestones (none remain) plus favourable rebate and discount estimate changes
Non-GAAP tax rate rose to 24.0% from 17.7%; full-year guide raised to 19% to 20%

catalysts.label: Lilly Q4 2026 earnings and 2027 guidance (date not confirmed; usually early February)
catalysts.note: Watch 2027 revenue guide, US price versus volume, and acquired IPR&D.

catalysts.label: Retatrutide BLA submission planned for Q1 2027

tripwires.text: Realised price decline worse than -15% in a quarter
tripwires.note: At the threshold: -15% in Q3 after -13% in Q2.
US price -7% in Q3 (Q2: -3%), partly offset by favourable rebate estimate changes.
Positive head-to-head Phase 3 in Q3; company still states Q1 2027.

risks: Government pricing action and wholesaler concentration; a new Congress sits from January 2027.
Compounded and competing GLP-1 products, and cheaper self-pay channels (Hims & Hers from November 2026).

lenses.eisman: Volume +53% with price -15%, and $900M of one-offs in the quarter: ask what growth looks like without rebate estimate changes and milestones.
lenses.munger: Invert it: what kills this? A US pricing reset that arrives faster than volume. US price went from -3% to -7% in one quarter.
lenses.buffett: Wonderful business, but he would refuse to underwrite a three-year price path he cannot see; the circle-of-competence test is hard.
lenses.hohn: Durable demand and pricing power are the test: price is falling faster, so durability rests on volume, Foundayo and retatrutide.

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q and release (quarter to 30 September 2026), with prices to the 13 November 2026 close; news reviewed to 16 November. Q4 and 2027 guidance come in early February; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: The incretin leader, growing 39% on one molecule. Volume is winning; US price fell 7% in Q3, and price and policy decide how long the premium lasts.
review.model: Lilly discovers, makes and sells branded medicines. Tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, is now the company.

how_it_earns.v: Incretins for diabetes and obesity. About two-thirds of Q3 revenue from Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo.
Verzenio for breast cancer plus newer launches. Flat to low growth.

mix.note: Revenue only: Lilly reports one segment, so profit by product is not disclosed. Cardiometabolic, Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience are Lilly's own groupings.

rows.label: Cardiometabolic
rows.driver: Volume +53% group-wide; price -15% on access deals, self-pay and China NRDL

rows.label: Oncology
rows.driver: Verzenio flat; newer launches add growth

review.position: One of two companies, with Novo Nordisk, that dominate obesity and diabetes incretins. Lilly is taking share: consensus has Novo's revenue falling in 2026 while Lilly's grows over a third.

moat.threat: Buyers are concentrated (PBMs, government). They take a growing share of the value through price.

what_numbers_say.t: Volume is doing all the work
what_numbers_say.d: Q3 revenue +39%: volume +53%, price -15%. US price -7% (Q2: -3%); outside the US price -29% on 76% more volume.
Non-GAAP gross margin 84.4% and GAAP 83.9%, below Q2. $4.2B of acquired IPR&D cut operating margin to about 35%.
Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo were about two-thirds of Q3 revenue. Any setback to tirzepatide hits the whole company.
About $900M of Q3 revenue was one-off: $410M of final Jardiance milestones plus favourable rebate and discount estimate changes.

balance.read: Leverage is low against EBITDA; debt fell in Q3 after rising $12.4B in H1 to fund deals.
facts: Total debt about $49.5B at 30 September (third-party tally), from $54.9B at 30 June
$18.2B of business development cash in nine months
Merida Biosciences acquired after quarter end

flags.evidence: Part of about $900M of Q3 one-off benefits came from favourable adjustments to rebate and discount estimates. Gross-to-net reserves are judgment calls.

flags.flag: Acquired IPR&D is large and recurring
flags.evidence: $4.2B in Q3 (AtaiBeckley, Curevo) after $2.8B in Q2. Lilly includes it in non-GAAP EPS, which is the conservative choice, but it makes EPS lumpy.
Jardiance price set from 2026; Trulicity and Verzenio selected, effective 2028 (IRA).

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Changed assumption: fades from 48% toward high teens as price cuts and comparisons bite
forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: operating leverage offset by price erosion
forecast_basis.share_chg: Trend: share count barely moves; buybacks offset dilution
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: growth premium narrows as growth slows

base.story: Volume keeps compounding as access widens; price erosion slows; growth fades to the high teens and the multiple compresses.
base.needs: US price decline stays within -8% a year; Foundayo and retatrutide launch on time

downside.story: Policy and competition reset US price faster than volume grows; the market re-rates Lilly toward big-pharma multiples.
downside.needs: US price falling more than 8% a year, or a safety or supply setback

upside.story: Oral and next-generation launches open new patients; price stabilises and growth stays above 30%.
upside.needs: Retatrutide approved in 2027 and Medicare obesity coverage made permanent

risks.cause: Price falls faster than volume grows
risks.how: Wider access (Medicare bridge, $299 Zepbound and $149 Foundayo self-pay, China NRDL) lowers price per dose. Q3 price was -15%; if volume growth slows first, revenue growth collapses.
Most-favoured-nation pricing and IRA negotiation pull US prices toward international levels. US price already fell 7% in Q3.
Novo's next-generation and oral products, and illegal compounded copies, compete for the same patients.
65% of revenue is tirzepatide. A safety signal, supply problem or patent challenge would hit everything at once.
Debt-funded acquisitions are expensed as IPR&D. If the programmes fail, the cash is gone and leverage stays higher.

peer_read.why_premium: Lilly is the only large pharma growing revenue above 30%, with the highest EBITDA margin and return on capital in the group.
peer_read.why_not: Novo Nordisk sells the same class of drug at well under half of Lilly's forward P/E because its growth has stalled. That gap shows how much of Lilly's value depends on continued share gains.
peer_read.peers_note: Novo reports in DKK; ratios are computed in DKK and sizes converted to USD. Trailing pharma P/Es are distorted by acquired IPR&D, so NTM is the cleaner read.

questions: How much of the 7% US price decline is policy, and how much is Lilly buying volume through self-pay?
Strip out $900M of one-offs: what is underlying growth?
Would you own this at Novo's multiple if growth halved?

review.title: Winning on volume, exposed on price
review.lead: We rate Eli Lilly {rating} with a 12-month target of {pt} ({upside} upside, {ret} total return against a cost of equity of {hurdle}). Lilly is winning the incretin market on volume and just raised revenue guidance by $5.5B, but US price per dose fell 7% in Q3 and our next-year EPS is {vs_cons} consensus: the shares already discount much of the good news.
review.call_reason: Leadership is priced in: the target implies {ret} over 12 months against a cost of equity of {hurdle}, with a fat tail if US prices reset.

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Q3 revenue grew 39% on 53% more volume and 15% lower prices. Mounjaro and Zepbound alone were $16.1B of $24.4B: the growth is real, but it rests on one molecule, and about $900M of the quarter was one-off.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Patents, injectable manufacturing scale and a deep follow-on pipeline (Foundayo launching globally, retatrutide beating Ozempic head to head with a filing planned for Q1 2027) keep Lilly ahead. Buyers and governments, not rivals, are the weak spot.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 84.4% and $4.2B of acquired IPR&D cut operating margin to about 35%. Operating leverage stays strong for as long as volume grows faster than price falls.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Lilly spent $18.2B on business development in nine months and expenses much of it as acquired IPR&D. Debt fell back to about $49.5B in Q3 and leverage is low against EBITDA, but more of the growth is now bought.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} Novo Nordisk sells the same class of drug at well under half of Lilly's forward P/E because its growth has stalled.

thesis_long: Lilly has won the first round of the obesity and diabetes market. Volume grew 53% in Q3, revenue outside the US rose 47%, and 2026 revenue guidance has now been raised three times, to $91B to $92B. Foundayo is launching, retatrutide beat Ozempic head to head, and newer products outside incretins doubled. On execution there is little to criticise.

The debate is price. Realised prices fell 15% in Q3, and US prices fell 7%, more than double Q2's decline. Access is widening in ways that lower price per dose: $299 a month self-pay Zepbound, $149 Foundayo, the Medicare bridge, and from November a direct channel on Hims & Hers. About $900M of Q3 revenue came from one-offs including rebate estimate changes, and government price-setting for Trulicity and Verzenio starts in 2028.

Our base case fades revenue growth to the high teens and lets the multiple compress toward large-pharma levels, which leaves 12-month returns close to the cost of equity. The upside case needs Foundayo and retatrutide to open new patient groups while US price settles near today's decline; the downside is a US price reset that arrives before volume growth slows. A US realised price decline worse than 8% a year, or a retatrutide delay, would turn us negative.

upside_risks.cause: Price settles while volume keeps compounding
upside_risks.how: If US price declines hold near -7% as access widens, revenue growth stays above 30% and EPS runs well ahead of our base case.
Permanent coverage beyond the bridge programme would add a large, durable patient pool.

dcf.label: EPS. Capex is not split out in our cash flow data for Lilly, and new manufacturing plants hold free cash flow below earnings

variant_view.why: We assume price erosion widens (US price went from -3% in Q2 to -7% in Q3) and fades revenue growth toward the high teens; consensus has 2027 EPS growth near 40% from this year's IPR&D-depressed base.

proof.event: Q4 2026 results and 2027 guidance (date not confirmed)
